Figure 14: Why raw trajectory underperforms on Wikipedia. (a) Context length over exploration steps, averaged across all 6 models (shaded bands: ±0.3 std): raw trajectory grows nearly linearly, while deduplicated trajectory and oracle belief remain more compact. (b) Query diversity over steps. This more directly reflects raw trajectory’s early coverage saturation: diversity drops sharply over steps 0–2, then decays at a similar rate but from a lower offset. deduplicated trajectory and oracle belief have similar diversity despite oracle belief’s higher coverage, indicating that novelty alone does not explain the oracle belief gain.

Figure 1: Information seeking under partial observability and its SeekerGym instantiation. (a) Under partial observability, a researcher iteratively asks questions or forms hypotheses, gathers evidence, updates a working belief shaped by curiosity and remaining uncertainty, and decides whether their understanding is sufficient to stop or whether further exploration is needed. (b) SeekerGym instantiates this generic loop as a benchmark pipeline (Algorithm 3): the Seeker issues a query at, the Retriever returns passages ot, the Belief Encoder updates the belief state bt+1, and the agent either continues or stops.

Figure 2: SeekerGym overview. (a) Retrieval Process. Wikipedia articles are parsed into passages and indexed via embed(·). Given a query at, the Retriever performs vector search over the passage index and returns all goal passages whose embedding similarity to at exceeds threshold θ as the observation ot. (b) Belief Representations. Three representations of the belief state bt: raw trajectory (btrajectory) preserves the verbatim query–observation history; deduplicated trajectory (bdeduplicated) retains only unique retrieved passages; oracle belief (boracle) uses the ground-truth article structure (GT Article), placing retrieved passages at their correct positions and marking unretrieved passages as [MISSING]. (c) Calibration Process (Algorithms 1, 2). Synthetic belief states {bs}n s=1 are fed to a completeness estimator to obtain predictions {ĉs}n s=1; nonconformity scores es = |cs − ĉs| against true completeness ratios {cs}n s=1 yield the calibration adjustment q̂. Passages shown in gray boxes are hidden from the estimator and are used only to define the true completeness ratio. (d) Inference. Given a deduplicated trajectory belief bt, the estimator produces ĉ from the visible passages only; the agent terminates (done) when ĉ− q̂ ≥ δ, guaranteeing 1−α coverage.
